stories.title: Zambians Vote in Presidential Election Amid Economic Concerns
stories.summary: Zambians voted on Thursday in a presidential election that tests the economic reforms of incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema. Approximately 8 million registered voters also selected members of Parliament and local councilors. Vote counting is currently underway, with results expected on Monday.

stories.title: Zambia Halts Vote Counting Amid Violence and Ballot Theft Reports
stories.summary: Zambia's electoral commission has suspended the counting of votes from the recent presidential and parliamentary elections due to violence directed at polling staff and reports of stolen marked ballots. The commission plans to reassess the situation within 24 hours. The main opposition candidate has expressed concern over the delays in the vote counting process.

stories.title: Nigel Farage Wins Clacton By-Election Against Count Binface
stories.summary: Nigel Farage, leader of the Reform UK party, won the Clacton by-election with 63% of the vote, defeating novelty candidate Count Binface, who received 27%. The election was criticized by major parties as a stunt, and Farage reportedly skipped the vote count due to security concerns following a credible threat against him. This election was triggered by Farage's resignation from the seat a month prior.

stories.title: Activists Attempt to Deliver Supplies to Besieged Families in Qusra
stories.summary: Activists attempted to deliver supplies to Palestinian families besieged by Israeli settlers in the village of Qusra, where three homes have been under siege for nearly a week. The Israeli military was deployed to the area, preventing the activists' efforts. Reports indicate that about 15 Palestinians, including children, are trapped in these homes, while Israeli troops have reportedly instructed families to evacuate their residences.

stories.title: Karoline Leavitt to Depart as White House Press Secretary, Succession Speculation Begins
stories.summary: Karoline Leavitt is set to leave her position as White House Press Secretary at the end of the month, as announced by President Trump. Leavitt, who recently returned from maternity leave, cited a desire to spend more time with her family as the reason for her departure. Speculation is already underway regarding potential candidates to succeed her, although the White House has not confirmed any names.

stories.title: US Missionary Kevin Rideout Released After Kidnapping in Niger
stories.summary: Kevin Rideout, an American missionary kidnapped in Niger last October, has been released after nine months in captivity. He is reported to be in good health and is currently in the care of US officials. His organization, SIM International, stated that he would soon be reunited with his family.

stories.title: Severe Rainfall in Japan Causes Fatalities and Strands Thousands
stories.summary: Unprecedented rainfall in Japan's Chiba prefecture has resulted in at least four fatalities and left approximately 7,000 passengers stranded at Tokyo's Narita airport. Authorities issued the highest-level rain warning for the first time, prompting evacuation orders for around 400,000 residents due to flooding risks and landslide alerts. Power outages affected over 20,000 households as the torrential rains continued to impact the region.

stories.title: Luigi Mangione Expected to Plead Guilty in Case Involving CEO's Death
stories.summary: Luigi Mangione is anticipated to plead guilty in federal court to charges related to the stalking and killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. The hearing is set for today, and discussions about a potential plea deal are ongoing. Mangione faces significant penalties, including life imprisonment, if he is found guilty on federal charges, which may also impact his state murder charges due to double jeopardy concerns.

stories.title: Kennedy Center Board Votes to Reinstate Trump's Name Amid Legal Challenges
stories.summary: The Kennedy Center's board of trustees has voted to restore Donald Trump's name on the building's facade, despite a previous court order mandating its removal. This decision also includes plans for a two-year renovation of the main building while keeping a smaller addition open. The move may lead to further legal disputes regarding the center's naming and future.

stories.title: USS George Washington Deploys to Middle East Amid Concerns Over USS Lincoln's Conditions
stories.summary: The USS George Washington aircraft carrier is en route to the Middle East to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has faced reports of declining mental health and supply issues among its crew during its record 260-day deployment. Some sailors aboard the Lincoln have reportedly attempted self-harm due to the conditions. However, U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has disputed these reports, calling them misrepresented, and senators are calling for an investigation into the situation.

stories.title: Wildfire in France Forces Evacuation of 525 Residents in Landes Region
stories.summary: A wildfire in the Landes region of southwestern France has led to the evacuation of 525 people from the village of Luglon. The fire has burned approximately 1,100 hectares of drought-affected pine forest and is advancing towards the village center. This incident is part of an unprecedented wildfire season in the area.

stories.title: Romania Shuts Down Nuclear Plant's Second Reactor Due to Low Danube Water Levels
stories.summary: Romania has begun the shutdown of the Cernavodă nuclear plant's second reactor as record low water levels in the Danube River hinder cooling operations. This follows the closure of the plant's first reactor in late July, attributed to scorching heat and insufficient rainfall. The plant, which supplies 20% of Romania's electricity, is not expected to resume operations within the next 10 days.

stories.title: Lawsuit Against Harvard Over Antisemitism Dismissed by Judge
stories.summary: A U.S. District Judge dismissed a lawsuit from the Trump administration alleging that Harvard University failed to protect Jewish students from antisemitism. The judge stated that the administration did not demonstrate an ongoing violation of federal civil rights laws, describing the alleged incidents as 'too isolated and episodic' to support the claims made in the lawsuit.

stories.title: Ebola Outbreak in DRC Expands to Sixth Province Amid Rising Death Toll
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has now spread to a sixth province, Bas-Uele, following the death of a man who traveled from Haut-Uele. The World Health Organization has indicated that this outbreak is on track to become the deadliest in history, surpassing the previous record of over 11,000 fatalities from a decade ago. Currently, more than 2,100 deaths have been reported out of over 4,500 cases.
